text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000086 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity tier, including simple acute visits, but the few charts returned support the billed levels, so documentation is too thin to settle the question.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is concerning: the 99215 share exceeds the all-provider rate in every complexity stratum, including patients with zero or one condition. Sampled low-complexity 99215s carry routine acute diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection, rash, UTI and unspecified abdominal pain (e.g., C0049062, C0049251, C0049818, C0049421, C0049590 is not in the packet so is excluded, C0048590), which is not what a sicker panel alone would explain; the overall mix is also heavily concentrated at 99214. Against that, the three documented 99215s (C0049632, C0049778, C0049985) and all documented 99213/99214 claims support the billed level. With records for only a small share of claims, that support is too thin to clear or confirm the pattern. The data-reviewed signal (a few moderate-plus notes with no lab or test line) is weak and could reflect cloned templates, but it is not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the 0-condition acute visits, and check whether MDM and time are individualized or templated."}
